subject.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args

question: Should the cron agent tool permanently advertise and repair flat `model`, `fallbacks`, and `toolsAllow` inputs while relying on downstream provider and tool-policy validation as the authoritative boundary?
rationale: The patch and proof are strong, but these fields influence provider routing and scheduled-agent tool authorization, so repository policy requires explicit owner intent rather than an automated merge judgment.

options.title: Accept the flat boundary
options.body: Merge after confirming downstream provider, credential, model, and toolsAllow enforcement remains authoritative for both nested and repaired flat calls.

options.title: Narrow sensitive fields
options.body: Keep flat schedule and payload-shape recovery but remove model, fallbacks, and toolsAllow from the advertised parallel surface.

options.title: Retain nested-only API
options.body: Decline the parallel flat contract and pursue better nested-schema descriptions or validation feedback instead.

recommendation.title: Accept the flat boundary
recommendation.body: Merge after confirming downstream provider, credential, model, and toolsAllow enforcement remains authoritative for both nested and repaired flat calls.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work directly touched the same cron agent-tool and session-target behavior, making this the closest available decision owner.
